transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-12
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood CSM), Marcus Lee (BrightBeam ML), Sofia Ruiz (BrightBeam DS), Nadia Patel (BrightBeam CTO), Evan Ortiz (BrightBeam Infra)

Summary: weekly POC sync; focussing on quantization experiments (INT8 vs FP8) run last week on BrightBeam summarization model. Quick review of quality metrics, perf deltas, and next steps. Some noisy transcripty bits below.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, uh quick check  everyone's here?
[00:06] Marcus: yeah here, sorry I was grabbing coffee,
[00:09] Nadia: here,
[00:10] Sofia: present,
[00:12] Alex: cool, ok so goal for today two things: one review the INT8 vs FP8 results you ran, and two agree on the next longer stability run and config changes. Priya is gonna walk through the metrics she pulled.
[00:26] Priya: yep, thanks Alex. so we ran the three main variants: FP16 baseline, FP8 mixed, and the INT8 quantized run with per-channel calibration. The workload was the 10k-document summarization set you provided, 512 token prompts, ~1k token outputs on average.
[00:44] Sofia: quick note real quick  we focused on the "legal" prompt subset and the internal docs subset since those were most sensitive to hallucinations.
[00:52] Priya: right, ok numbers  quality first: ROUGE-L averaged 0.42 for FP16, 0.41 for FP8 (so ~2.4% relative drop), and 0.39 for INT8 (~7% relative drop vs FP16). We also looked at an extractive overlap score and exact-match on a labeled subset: exact-match dropped from 72% (FP16) to 69% (FP8) to 64% (INT8).
[01:26] Marcus: those numbers are close to what we feared but still maybe tolerable depending on the edge cases  the legal subset had a bigger drop for INT8, more hallucinations on citations.
[01:36] Priya: yeah we saw hallucination increase on the legal prompts with INT8; FP8 mostly preserved factuality but some tokenization edge cases popped.
[01:45] Alex: can you explain the INT8 calibration you used? was it per-channel, and did you do ACIQ-style or post-training calibration with a small dataset?
[01:55] Priya: per-channel quant with 512-sample calibration set drawn from your validation shard. We used per-layer clipping and a small symmetric quant scheme. Did not use learned quantization (e.g., QAT). We can try QAT but that changes workflow.
[02:11] Nadia: how about latency numbers  we care about p95 and throughput for our live dedupe pipeline.
[02:17] Priya: latency end-to-end (model only) averaged: FP16: 420ms p50 / 680ms p95; FP8: 380ms p50 / 610ms p95; INT8: 310ms p50 / 480ms p95. Throughput (tokens/sec) on the test GPU (A10x cluster)  FP16 ~1200 tokens/s, FP8 ~1450 tokens/s, INT8 ~1900 tokens/s.
[02:46] Evan: those are big throughput wins for INT8, nice. what about memory and KV cache size?
[02:50] Priya: memory footprint reduced ~35% INT8 vs FP16; KV cache memory similarly smaller which helped latency on longer sequences.
[02:59] Marcus: so cost delta? assumed token-cost reduction roughly proportional to GPU hours but also accounting for batch size differences.
[03:07] Alex: Priya has a cost sheet draft  Priya do you want to summarize the per-token cost deltas?
[03:12] Priya: yeah so on the test infra we saw ~40% lower GPU time per token with INT8 vs FP16; FP8 gave ~20% reduction. After accounting for slightly higher error rates (more retries for manual review on legal subset), net expected cost savings for production looked like 30% for INT8, 15% for FP8. I'll share the token-level csv after the call.
[03:34] Sofia: question  can we tune INT8 to recover some quality? like selective layer fallback or mixed precision on critical heads?
[03:42] Priya: absolutely  couple of levers: mixed per-layer precision (keep first n layers FP16, quantize rest), per-attention-head selective fallback, and calibration set composition. We tried one quick mixed run (first 4 layers FP16), that moved the ROUGE from 0.39 to 0.405 and reduced hallucinations by ~half on sample inspection but increased latency to ~340ms p50.
[04:03] Alex: good tradeoff  sounds like a middle ground we'd want to explore. Marcus, does that seem acceptable to BrightBeam?
[04:09] Marcus: yeah if we can get hallucination under control on the legal set and still keep ~25% cost reduction, that's a win.
[04:15] Nadia: also need to confirm SLOs for latency  we have an internal max p95 of 700ms so INT8 is fine, even with mixed layers.
[04:22] Evan: regarding ops  if we move to Dedicated, we need to validate the GPU type and driver stack. any surprises on kernel compatibility with our A10x cluster?
[04:33] Priya: we tested on a 5300 driver set; INT8 kernels used our optimized path which currently relies on cutlass/kernels aligned to 5300+. There were no crashes but one edge-case quant kernel logged a warning for a particular sequence length, which showed up in logs. We'll provide the exact kernel versions in the runbook.
[04:52] Jordan: quick prod-ops question  how are we handling model pinning and rollbacks if a quantized model regresses?
[04:57] Alex: Redwood supports model variants and automatic fallback; we can configure routing rules to send X% of traffic to FP16 if error rates spike, and then automatically roll back. We'll include the canary config in the runbook.
[05:09] Sofia: about hallucinations  do you have examples? we pulled a couple from INT8 where the model hallucinated a statute number.
[05:16] Priya: yeah we have two sample transcripts I uploaded to the shared drive: INT8_example_23.txt and FP16_baseline_23.txt, you can see the difference. We'll attach those to the benchmark sheet.
[05:25] Marcus: for the legal workflows we might need QAT or a small fine-tune on the calibration set  is that supported in the POC?
[05:31] Alex: we can run QAT in the POC but that increases cycle time. recommend doing more calibration and layer-selective quant first; if unacceptable, consider a small targeted fine-tune.
[05:42] Nadia: any security concerns with the calibration dataset? do we need to worry about PII in calibration samples?
[05:47] Priya: good call  we used redacted samples but please confirm the samples you gave us are cleared. Also Redwood's Private/Dedicated options provide customer-managed KMS for keys and audit logs if you want that for the POC.
[05:59] Evan: on VPC peering, we need to confirm egress and port rules  I'll send network requirements to Alex after call.
[06:06] Alex: perfect. OK next steps recap  Alex go over runbook and configs, Priya produce cost sheet, BrightBeam run 4-hour stability on INT8 with the mixed-layer config we discussed. Schedule follow-up.
[06:19] Marcus: timeline  we can run the 4-hour test next Monday, and send logs by Tuesday.
[06:25] Alex: great. Jordan will coordinate the follow-up meeting invite.
[06:29] Jordan: I'll put tentative 5/20 on calendar for demo and ops deep dive.
[06:33] Nadia: good.
[06:34] Alex: any other questions?
[06:36] Sofia: one minor  can you include the exact sampling and temperature settings you used for the runs?
[06:40] Priya: yes, temperature 0.0 for deterministic eval, top-k 50 for the production-like runs. I'll include config block.
[06:47] Alex: awesome. thanks everyone, we'll follow up on action items.

[End of recording]
